_why: PLAT-04, PLAT-01, PLAT-09. An ADDON LAYER's checks file. It lives beside the layer's script triple at labs/clusters/grid-core/addons/ops/checks.json, not at labs/mN/checks.json — that second path is the MODULE checks path C1 and C6 read for truth_contract, and a layer is not a module, so this file carries no Truth Contract tag at all. EVERY ENTRY ASSERTS OBJECT STATE, A FILE-LEVEL COUNT, OR A COMPONENT'S OWN STATE DOCUMENT, AND NONE ASSERTS A PERFORMANCE NUMBER: no latency, no scrape duration, no sample rate, no throughput, no percentage. AND NONE ASSERTS A COST FIGURE, which for this layer is the sharper half of the same rule — the cost tool runs with no cloud integration and no real pricing, so every rate it uses is a default standing in for a price nobody paid, and a figure derived from that is arithmetic over a fabricated rate. NO ENTRY ASSERTS A POD PHASE either, and here that is the load-bearing decision rather than a style rule: a metrics collector whose every scrape target is DOWN is Running, Ready and Available and has collected nothing, so a phase assertion cannot tell a working install from one that measured nothing. The three live entries therefore read the COLLECTOR'S own target state, the DASHBOARD'S own health endpoint (including the version it reports, because the pinned major is a forward schema contract the course's later dashboards are generated against) and the COST TOOL'S own readiness endpoint. FIVE ENTRIES NEED NO CLUSTER and each counts its own subjects, so a mis-pathed or truncated scan cannot satisfy one: the digest-pin count over the committed render, the register-versus-render agreement in both directions, the bundled-distribution ban, the dashboard-schema-contract pin, and the no-persistence assertion. ONE SCAN IS DELIBERATELY SCOPED AWAY FROM ITS OWN INSTRUMENT: the bundled-distribution ban scans the committed render and NOT the layer's scripts or PINS.md, because the excluded component names have to appear in create.sh's header and in the register's section 3 where the exclusion is explained with its budget arithmetic — a scan including them would hit its own explanation, which is the project's established narrow-or-reword resolution rather than an allowlist. EVERY kubectl RUN SETS KUBECONFIG ITSELF, measured on the base profile: create.sh exports KUBECONFIG=/tmp/grid-core.kubeconfig, but an export inside a script dies with the script, so the learner's own shell has no context and a bare `kubectl --context kind-grid-core` fails with `context was not found`.

checks.describe: PLAT-01 over the layer's own committed object set, and the first of the entries here that needs no cluster: every image reference in rendered-pinned.yaml carries an @sha256 digest. It COUNTS the references as well as the unpinned ones, so a render that lost its workloads — a truncated file, a mis-pathed scan — cannot satisfy it either. Each pin is a multi-architecture INDEX digest, so the same reference resolves on this arm64 host and on an amd64 runner, which is the property the CI matrix depends on
checks.run: cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*image:[[:space:]]*"\{0,1\}\([^"[:space:]][^"[:space:]]*\)"\{0,1\}[[:space:]]*$/\1/p' labs/clusters/grid-core/addons/ops/rendered-pinned.yaml | awk 'BEGIN{n=0;bad=0}{n++; if (index($0,"@sha256:")==0) bad++}END{printf "image_refs=%d unpinned=%d\n", n, bad}'

checks.describe: the entry that makes PINS.md load-bearing rather than decorative, and the one this layer needs more than any other in the phase: these four digests were resolved for the FIRST TIME in this plan, so there is no earlier artifact that would catch a register and a render drifting apart. It counts the digests the register records, counts how many of them appear in the committed render, and asserts the two counts are equal AND non-zero. A pin written in the register and absent from the manifest is a pin nobody applied; a digest in the manifest that the register does not record is a pin with no provenance. Both directions matter, which is why this is a comparison rather than a presence test
checks.run: cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && D=labs/clusters/grid-core/addons/ops && sed -n 's/^| `[^`]*@\(sha256:[0-9a-f]\{1,\}\)`.*$/\1/p' "$D/PINS.md" | sort -u | awk -v f="$D/rendered-pinned.yaml" 'BEGIN{n=0;hit=0} { n++; found=0; while ((getline line < f) > 0) { if (index(line,$0)>0) { found=1 } } ; close(f); if (found) hit++ } END{printf "registered=%d present_in_render=%d\n", n, hit}'

checks.describe: the layer installs three slim releases and NOT the bundled monitoring distribution, asserted over the APPLIED OBJECT SET rather than over any prose. The reason is measured and lives in PINS.md section 3: the declared-minimum lab budget is 4500 MiB, the base profile at rest with its three feature gates measures 1908 MiB, and the bundled distribution adds an operator with its custom resource definitions, an alert manager, a node exporter per node, a kube-state-metrics deployment and a default rule set. The scan looks for the operator's API group on apiVersion:/apiGroups: lines, and for the component names on the render's own OBJECT NAMES. It deliberately does NOT scan image references, and that narrowing was forced by a real false positive measured here: the collector's own config-reload sidecar is published under the operator's ORGANISATION path on its registry, so an image scan hit `quay.io/prometheus-operator/prometheus-config-reloader` — a legitimate sidecar of the slim release, not the operator. An installed component always creates objects NAMED for it, and the operator's custom resource definitions are caught by the group clause, so the narrowed form loses no coverage. It COUNTS the object kinds it walked past so a scan that read nothing cannot pass. SCOPED SET: rendered-pinned.yaml only, deliberately NOT the layer's scripts or PINS.md — the excluded names have to appear in create.sh's header and in the register's section 3 where the exclusion is explained, so a wider scan would hit its own explanation
checks.run: cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && awk 'BEGIN{k=0;h=0} /^[[:space:]]*#/ {next} /^kind:/ {k++} (/apiVersion:/ || /apiGroups:/) && /monitoring\.coreos\.com/ {h++} /^  name:/ && /alertmanager|node-exporter|kube-state-metrics|pushgateway|prometheus-operator/ {h++} END{printf "kinds=%d bundled_distribution=%d\n", k+0, h+0}' labs/clusters/grid-core/addons/ops/rendered-pinned.yaml

checks.describe: the forward schema contract, asserted where it can drift. The dashboard's major fixes the JSON schema a later phase's generated dashboards are authored against, and this layer OVERRIDES its chart's own appVersion to reach it — no published chart in that series ships the pinned major, so the pairing is not one upstream tests. This entry reads the major out of PINS.md section 4 and out of the dashboard image reference in the committed render and asserts they are the same number, so a values file edited without the register, or a register edited without the values file, fails here rather than in the phase whose dashboards stop rendering. The live half — the running instance REPORTING that major on its own health endpoint — is the verify entry below
checks.run: cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && D=labs/clusters/grid-core/addons/ops && P=$(sed -n 's/^\*\*Pinned: Grafana `\([0-9]\{1,\}\)\..*$/\1/p' "$D/PINS.md" | sed -n '1,1p') && R=$(sed -n 's|^[[:space:]]*image:[[:space:]]*"\{0,1\}[^"[:space:]]*grafana/grafana:\([0-9]\{1,\}\)\..*$|\1|p' "$D/rendered-pinned.yaml" | sed -n '1,1p') && printf 'register_major=%s render_major=%s\n' "${P:-none}" "${R:-none}"

checks.describe: persistence is off for all three components, asserted on the applied object set rather than remembered from the values file. A profile is torn down at the end of every lab, so a volume that outlives the cluster is state the Grid repository is supposed to carry instead — and for the cost tool specifically it would be a record of fabricated rates surviving the cluster that produced them. This is also what makes the teardown's missing deletion ORDER a decision rather than an omission: with no claim there is no finalizer waiting on another component. Counts the object kinds it walked past so a scan that read nothing cannot pass
checks.run: cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && awk 'BEGIN{k=0;h=0} /^[[:space:]]*#/ {next} /^kind:/ {k++; if ($2 == "PersistentVolumeClaim") h++} /persistentVolumeClaim:/ {h++} END{printf "kinds=%d persistent_claims=%d\n", k+0, h+0}' labs/clusters/grid-core/addons/ops/rendered-pinned.yaml

checks.describe: the live object-state entry, and the one that is asserted as a COUNT rather than as a per-name lookup so it cannot pass over an empty namespace. jq folds the three Deployments the layer applies and reports how many exist and how many have at least one available replica; the assert requires three of three. An absent namespace yields zero and fails, which is the correct answer for an un-applied layer — 'every workload is available' over zero workloads is vacuously true, and a verify that reports clean over an un-applied layer is this phase's named failure mode. No Pod phase is read: availableReplicas is the Deployment's own status, not a Pod's
checks.run: cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && KUBECONFIG="${KUBECONFIG:-/tmp/grid-core.kubeconfig}" kubectl --context kind-grid-core -n grid-ops get deploy -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '[.items[] | select(.metadata.name=="prometheus-server" or .metadata.name=="grafana" or .metadata.name=="opencost")] | "layer_workloads=" + (length|tostring) + " available=" + ([.[] | select((.status.availableReplicas // 0) >= 1)] | length | tostring)' || echo 'layer_workloads=0 available=0'

checks.describe: verify.sh exits 0 and its one OK: line says, in order, how many layer workloads are available, how many scrape targets the COLLECTOR ITSELF reports healthy out of how many, the version the DASHBOARD ITSELF reports against the pinned major, and that the COST TOOL answered its own readiness endpoint. The anchored pattern requires a NON-ZERO healthy-target count, which is the half a Pod-phase assertion cannot reach: a collector whose every target is down is Running, Ready and Available and has collected nothing. It also requires the dashboard's reported version and the pinned major to both appear, so the schema contract is visible in the line rather than only inside the script. No number in the pattern is a performance figure — they are counts of objects and of scrape targets

assert.matches: ^OK: addon-ops verified on 'grid-core' — 3/3 layer workloads available in 'grid-ops', the collector reports [1-9][0-9]* of [1-9][0-9]* scrape targets healthy from its OWN target state \(jobs: [^)]*\), the dashboard answers its own health endpoint reporting version [0-9.]+ against the pinned major [0-9]+, and the cost tool answers its own readiness endpoint\.$

checks.describe: the pin read back off the RUNNING containers rather than off the manifest, which is the half a written-only pin never catches: a manifest can ask for a digest and a node can resolve something else. It counts the digests PINS.md records and counts how many of them appear in some container's imageID as the kubelet reports it, and asserts the two are equal and non-zero. The same comparison runs inside create.sh on every apply and fails the install on a mismatch, so this entry is a record of an assertion that is enforced rather than a one-off observation
checks.run: cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && IDS=$(KUBECONFIG="${KUBECONFIG:-/tmp/grid-core.kubeconfig}" kubectl --context kind-grid-core -n grid-ops get pods -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '[.items[].status.containerStatuses[]?.imageID] | join(" ")') && sed -n 's/^| `[^`]*@\(sha256:[0-9a-f]\{1,\}\)`.*$/\1/p' labs/clusters/grid-core/addons/ops/PINS.md | sort -u | awk -v ids="$IDS" 'BEGIN{n=0;hit=0} { n++; if (index(ids,$0)>0) hit++ } END{printf "registered=%d honoured_by_a_running_container=%d\n", n, hit}'
